# Ra (`ra` CLI) session fixtures

Raw on-disk fixtures for `parsers::ra::RaParser`, mirroring Ra's
real storage layout. Read them with a parser pointed at this directory:

```rust
let parser = RaParser::with_base_dir(
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/fixtures/recur"),
);
```

The parser `WalkDir`s `<base>/**/*.jsonl`, so both the canonical (`users/…`)
and legacy-flat (`sessions/…`) trees below are picked up from the one call.

## Data root

`RA_HOME`, else `~/.ra` (Windows: `C:\Users\<you>\.ra`). This directory stands
in for that root. Note what the root is **not**: there is no `agent/`
subdirectory, and no pi-style `settings.json` / `auth.json` pair. Ra
keeps its config in `<root>/config.json` plus `<root>/profiles/<id>.json`.

## Layouts

| Layout | Path |
| --- | --- |
| legacy flat | `<root>/sessions/{enc(session_key)}.jsonl` |
| canonical per-user | `<root>/users/{enc(base_key)}/sessions/{enc(topic)}.jsonl` |
| per-profile | `<root>/profiles/<id>/data/sessions/…`, `<root>/profiles/<id>/data/users/<base>/sessions/…` |

`topic` defaults to `default`. No per-profile fixture is committed here — those
trees are the same shape as the two layouts above, nested one level deeper.

## Filename percent-encoding

Keep ASCII alphanumerics, `-` and `_`; every other byte becomes `%{HEX:02X}`
(uppercase), so `:` → `%3A` and a session key `proj-alpha:u1` names the
directory `proj-alpha%3Au1`. Keys longer than 200 chars get a
`_{fnv1a64_hash:016X}` suffix appended before encoding.

## Line schema

Line 1 is a `SessionMeta` header; the rest are `Message` rows or control
records. Both are snake_case, and a `Message` carries **no** discriminating
`type`/`kind` tag — `role` is a plain lowercase string.

`SessionMeta`: `schema_version`, `session_key`, `created_at`, `updated_at`,
`sealed_segments`, and optionally `topic`, `title`, `summary`, `parent_key`,
`base_seq`, `title_manual`, `child_contracts`.

`Message`: `role` (`user` | `assistant` | `tool` | `system`), `content` (a
string), `timestamp`, and optionally `tool_calls`
(`[{ id, name, arguments, metadata? }]`), `tool_call_id`, `reasoning_content`,
`media`, `client_message_id`, `thread_id`.

Thread linking: a user row's `thread_id` equals its own `client_message_id`;
the assistant and tool rows of that turn reuse the same `thread_id`. An
assistant that calls a tool has `tool_calls` and may have empty `content`; its
result arrives as a separate `role: "tool"` row carrying `tool_call_id`.

Control record: `{ "kind": "rollback", "num_turns": N, "at": "<RFC3339>" }`. A
faithful reader drops the last `N` user turns up to that point, so a transcript
containing one is not read as its raw line count.

## Files

| Path | Session key | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `users/proj-alpha%3Au1/sessions/default.jsonl` | `proj-alpha:u1` | plain user → assistant text exchange |
| `users/proj-beta%3Au2/sessions/default.jsonl` | `proj-beta:u2` | `tool_calls` with empty `content`, matching `role: "tool"` result, final assistant text |
| `users/proj-gamma%3Au3/sessions/default.jsonl` | `proj-gamma:u3` | assistant `reasoning_content` |
| `users/proj-delta%3Au4/sessions/default.jsonl` | `proj-delta:u4` | three turns, three distinct `thread_id`s |
| `users/proj-rollback%3Au5/sessions/default.jsonl` | `proj-rollback:u5` | mid-file `rollback` control record (`num_turns: 1`) |
| `sessions/legacy%3Asimple.jsonl` | `legacy:simple` | legacy flat layout |

Timestamps increase within every file, and each header's `updated_at` equals
its last message's `timestamp`.

Regenerated by a one-off script; edit the JSON lines in place if you need
another shape. Keep them one-object-per-line (no pretty-printing) — the format
is JSONL.
